clauses.reason: Enacting words: the President acts under the Constitution and laws and orders what follows. The lead carries no command of its own; it supports the sections that follow and ends with them. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 26, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-12-26, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 26, 2025 begins.

Section 1 closes all executive departments and agencies of the Federal Government and excuses their employees from duty on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 ("shall be closed and their employees excused from duty on Wednesday,"). The text identifies the two days as the day before and the day following Christmas Day, respectively. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 26, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-12-26, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 26, 2025 begins.

Section 2 lets the heads of departments and agencies decide that certain offices and installations must remain open and that certain employees must report for duty on the closed days, for reasons of national security, defense, or other public need ("December 24, 2025, or December 26, 2025, or both, for reasons of national"). It is a discretion that attaches to the closure in section 1 and has no operation once the closed days are over. The first end is the order's own terms with no later act needed: the order operates on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 only, and nothing in its text continues any command past December 26, 2025. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-12-26, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 26, 2025 begins.

Section 3 provides that the closed days shall be considered as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, and of 5 U.S.C. 5546 and 6103(b) and other similar statutes insofar as they relate to the pay and leave of employees ("as falling within the scope of Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971,"). It is a deeming rule for the closed days only. Executive Order 11582 is an earlier order cited as the pay-and-leave framework; it is not a later event and does not end this order. The pay and leave consequences for the closed days are recorded under savings. The order has no effective-date wording of its own that postpones the day, so the end is recorded as the last day named, 2025-12-26, inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the alternative exclusive reading would end it when December 26, 2025 begins.

Section 4 directs the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to take such actions as may be necessary to implement the order ("such actions as may be necessary to implement this order."). It is an implementation command with no stated date and no held record of what the Director did or when. It implements only the closure and excusal for Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025, so it is read as having no operation after December 26, 2025; that reading is an inference from the order's text and is disclosed, and it does not rest on any completion date. Section 5(d) provides that the costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Office of Personnel Management. It allocates one cost, the cost of publishing the order, which the held Federal Register text shows was published on December 23, 2025 (90 FR 60545-60546). The clause is read as spent on that publication date, 2025-12-23, because publication is the event whose cost it allocates; no held source gives the date any bill was paid, so that reading is disclosed. It ends before the closed days do, and the whole-order end stays 2025-12-26.

The heading, number, title (Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on December 24, 2025, and December 26, 2025) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text. It has sections 1 to 5 (section 5 with its sub-items), a lead paragraph and section 5(d) on publication costs; the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the order closes the departments and agencies on Wednesday, December 24, 2025, and Friday, December 26, 2025 and says nothing that runs past December 26, 2025, so every clause ends by the order's own terms on 2025-12-26 (section 5(d) excepted where it is dated separately). No later instrument names the order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text, and the dossier's later-event chain is empty. The only other instrument the text names is Executive Order 11582 of February 11, 1971, an earlier order cited in section 3.
